Run the housekeeping that is due, for example from cron

Without a subcommand, maintain sweeps, retires, compacts and builds presence filters. It collects garbage once the last collection is older than --gc-interval. It also rebuilds the database indexes of heavily changed tables in the index. A subcommand runs one of these operations. A store server runs this housekeeping on its own schedule.

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain [flags] <command>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--gc-interval value` | collect garbage when the last collection is at least this old; 0 turns collection off |  | `168h0m0s` |

## maintain sweep

Finalize idle archives and end sessions whose lease has expired

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain sweep
```

## maintain compact

Rewrite small archives into full-sized ones

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain compact
```

## maintain retire

Tombstone the retired commits whose trash window has ended

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain retire
```

## maintain presence

Build a presence filter for each set whose newest commit lacks one

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain presence
```

## maintain check

Report the commits in the store that are missing from the index and not tombstoned

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain check
```

## maintain sizes

Record the logical size of commits that lack one; measure the sets whose commits changed

```sh
goback [global flags] maintain sizes
```
